title: The detective, a friend's $300 loan and the held trunk
summary: The act skips its spot, a detective confronts Bubbles, and a Chicago usher friend lends $300 to get to New York while the manager keeps the trunk.

"You come down like somebody starting something, I ain't starting nothing." So while he's standing there he's telling me don't you all do so-and-so, don't you do so-and-so, I'm going back upstairs and leave him down there. This is in the basement of the theater, you know.
So I go back upstairs and while upstairs I thought I'd walk around to this place

where this girl is. Her name -- her name -- her name -- oh, I'll think of it. However, I go around to the theater where she was working, which is only a couple of blocks around from where I am or where I was, and I tell her the story, told her why I didn't call, I told her we quit the act and left so-and-so and-so, and I need some money to get back to New York 'cause I didn't have but 25 cents in my pocket. So she goes in her little kitty and gets out $300 for Buck and I to go to New York, give it to me. And we go back to the theater and the manager wanted to keep the trunk. All of our clothes were in the trunk. Street clothes, stage clothes and all in this trunk, you know. So he didn't let us have the trunk. Okay.
